SQLite locking: Anki holds exclusive lock while open - cannot write concurrently. Workaround: copy DB for reads, or use AnkiConnect which serializes access through Anki process.

Official anki Python package (pip install anki) supports headless collection access without GUI. Provides Collection class for CRUD, search, scheduling, import. Writes go through proper sync-aware methods. Can import CSV/apkg programmatically.

Concurrency: Anki holds SQLite lock while running. Direct DB access while Anki open = SQLITE_BUSY errors. AnkiConnect serializes all requests through Anki main thread, making it safe. Multiple agents should funnel through single AnkiConnect endpoint.

Card identity: .apkg import uses GUID for matching (same GUID + same model fields = overwrite). Text/CSV import uses first field matching. genanki default GUID = hash of all fields; override with guid_for() for stable identity. Critical: model fields must match for GUID-based update to work.

GUID CRITICAL: genanki default GUID = hash(all fields). When content changes, GUID changes, causing DUPLICATE instead of UPDATE on reimport. Must override genanki.Note.guid with deterministic hash of STABLE IDENTITY FIELDS ONLY (e.g., deck_id+card_index).

AnkiConnect processes requests serially due to GIL - no true parallel execution. Multiple simultaneous HTTP requests queue up. The anki pip package can be used headlessly without GUI (pip install anki). apyanki/apy are CLI tools using it. headless-anki Docker images exist for CI/containerized use.

AnkiConnect processes requests serially (Python GIL + Qt main thread). Safe from race conditions but slow for bulk ops. SQLite allows only one writer at a time. Direct DB manipulation while Anki is open causes database locked errors.

Official anki Python package (pip install anki) can open collection.anki2 directly for CLI use. But CANNOT be used while Anki desktop is running (same SQLite file). Good for batch operations when Anki is closed.

ankisync2 library (91 stars): peewee ORM wrapper for .apkg/.anki2 SQLite manipulation. Supports creating, reading, updating notes inside packages. But author warns: not safe for live collection while Anki is running. Best for offline .apkg generation/editing.

AnkiConnect has NO rate limiting - processes requests sequentially through Qt event loop. No concurrent access issues because all requests are serialized by Anki desktop process. Auth via apiKey config (optional). The multi action enables batching multiple operations in single HTTP call.

importPackage via AnkiConnect: file must be in collection.media folder. Anki apkg import identifies notes by matching note ID - if newer, updates content. Option to include/exclude scheduling. Default behavior: updates notes in-place preserving scheduling, does NOT reset review progress.

APKG import update behavior confirmed: When importing .apkg, Anki identifies notes already in collection by GUID. If file notes are NEWER than local copy, they get updated. Scheduling is preserved for existing cards. importPackage AnkiConnect action wraps this same behavior.

CRITICAL: genanki GUID is hash of ALL fields by default. If you change any field content, GUID changes, causing duplicates on reimport. Must override guid property to hash only identity fields (e.g. first field or a unique ID). genanki.guid_for(*args) hashes its args to produce a stable base91 GUID.

CONFIRMED: genanki.Note guid override pattern is official and documented in genanki README. Use 'class StableNote(genanki.Note): @property def guid(self): return genanki.guid_for(identity_key)'. This is the canonical fix.

CONFIRMED: importPackage preserves scheduling. Anki compares mod timestamp: if imported note mod > local mod, it updates fields while keeping card intervals/due dates/ease/reps/lapses. No delete needed with stable GUIDs.
